Reasoning:

The request asks to "skip planning" and just emit 20 columns + configs. I will comply with the deliverable (a concrete 20-column plan with configs), but I cannot silently drop the two things that determine whether this study is even answerable: driver feasibility and validation.

Goals decompose into (1) a mechanistic goal — explain how water partitioning (ET vs surface runoff vs sub-surface drainage) varies across Naches's heterogeneity, and (2) a validation goal — which is DEAD ON ARRIVAL here because `observations_available` is empty. I cannot validate partitioning against nothing, so all 20 columns become exploratory and I flag validation as a gap.

Drivers are elevation and soil. Naches has ~1625 m relief, and the CONUS default NLDAS-2 forcing (~12 km) DOES vary orographically, so elevation acts on precipitation/temperature/snow with real (if coarse) signal — elevation is PARTIALLY answerable (snow/SWE is in default output). The honest caveat: sub-12 km terrain is unresolved, so ridgetop snow will be underestimated and adjacent columns can share a forcing cell. Soil is fully answerable via SSURGO per column. Partitioning includes drainage/recharge (slow states), so a WTD-informed warm start is required or ZWT/QDRAI are init artifacts.

N=20 is user-imposed, not derived; I justify it as 4 elevation bands × ~2 soil classes with light replication, weighted toward the rain-snow transition where snowmelt-driven partitioning is most sensitive. Elevation-band and soil assignments here REQUIRE downstream DEM and SSURGO sampling — the coordinates below span the west(high)→east(low) gradient but their band labels are intent, not measured.
